To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the structure functions and the flame surface density conditioned on different mixture fractions and reaction progress variables are significantly affected by the heat release induced by combustion, and that the flame normal gradient conditioned on the tangential velocity is significant and increases with increasing turbulence intensities.

the heat release due to the combustion can significantly affect the second order structure functions conditioned on different mixture conditions, the magnitude of the tangential flame normal gradient of velocity can be non-negligible, and the baroclinicity can have significant effects on the second order structure function conditioned on the heat release zone for turbulent premixed flames belonging to the wrinkle flamelet and corr
the structure functions and the components conditioned on different flame states exhibit different statistical behaviors, and that these behaviors are affected by the turbulence intensity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of heat release on the structure of turbulent premixed flames.
the statistical properties of conditioned second order structure functions for turbulent premixed flames.
the statistical analysis of the conditioned second order structure functions of velocity fluctuations in turbulent premixed combustion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the effects of the heat release on the second order structure functions of the velocity conditioned on different mixture fractions and their components are more significant than those of the turbulence intensity and the Karlovitz number.
the structure functions conditioned to the heat release zone are affected by the combustion induced thermal expansion and the anisotropic baroclinic effect.

the statistical behaviors of the conditioned second order structure functions are significantly influenced by the heat release due to the combustion and the anisotropic baroclinic effects induced by the flame brush, and the density weighted velocities do not reduce the scatter in the magnitude of the structure functions conditioned to various events.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the second order structure functions can be used as an effective tool to investigate the effects of combustion on turbulence and vice versa.

the effects of the heat release on the structure functions conditioned to the reactant mixture state are not negligible, even for the flames belonging the thin reaction zone regime, and the anisotropic influences of the baroclinicity can be significant for the flames belonging in the wrinkled flamelets and corrugated flames regimes.
the structure functions conditioned to various mixture states can be used as an effective tool to understand the underlying physical phenomena in turbulent combustion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structure functions and the structure functions components conditioned on various mixture states are sensitive to the combustion induced thermal expansion and the baroclinicity effects.

the conditional structure functions can be used to gain insight into the effects of the local mixture states on the turbulent transport of the velocity field and to quantify the anisotropic influences of the flame on the velocity fluctuations.
the effects of heat release on the conditioned second order statistics are significant, and these effects are not reduced by density weighting the velocity.
